🧳 External / portable drive · 🪫 Won't power on / dead

External Hard Drive Not Spinning or Won't Power On

If an external drive has no lights or sound, the cause may be a bad cable, a dead power adapter, a failed bridge board, or a failed drive. A burnt smell suggests an electrical fault, so stop trying.

4/5 · High risk
Success odds: Low

Cable and adapter checks are safe, but repeated attempts on a drive with an electrical or motor fault can make things worse.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Unplug it if you smell burning or see scorch marks. Do not power it up again.
  • Do not keep power-cycling it hoping it starts.
  • Do not use the freezer trick, and never open the drive. It needs a cleanroom.
  • Do not use a power adapter that does not match the one it came with. The wrong voltage can burn the board.

🧑‍🔧 When to call a pro

If there are no lights or spin after good cable and power checks, or there is a burnt smell, stop and use a professional.

Questions people ask

No lights at all. Is the drive dead?

Not necessarily. A broken cable, adapter, USB port or bridge board can look the same. Try other cables and computers before giving up.

Can I take the drive out and connect it directly?

Only if it has a standard SATA connector and is not encrypted by the enclosure. Many portables do not, so check the model first.

Is a loose USB port fixable?

It can be, but soldering needs skill, and a poor repair can damage the board. Ask an expert for valuable data.

Before you start: Educational DIY guide, no warranty. DIY recovery can cause permanent data loss. If the data is valuable, consider a professional first.
